findings: The three displayed reactions are chemically balanced and use the correct subscripts: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (Brennen), CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ (Löschen), and Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O (Abbinden). The carbonate appears as the starting material and the product of setting.

The two left arrows carry the process from burning to slaking to setting; the right arrow returns from setting to burning. Each arrowhead points in the intended cycle direction. CO₂ leaving the kiln, water added during slaking, and CO₂ entering the setting material are depicted consistently with the equations.

The actual 360x203 and 680x383 previews were inspected. All three complete equations, including the ₂/₃ indices and Ca(OH)₂ parentheses, remain distinguishable at 360 pixels. In the active JPG viewed at 360 pixels, the long setting equation and indices are too small to read reliably. The new horizontal three-row layout fixes that documented weakness.

The rounded red, blue and green panels, simple kiln, water and masonry motifs, and warm palette retain the friendly comic-like character of the current asset. The 1672x941 PNG is near 16:9 and has no necessary small explanatory text beyond the enlarged equations.
scopeLimit: Candidate inspection only. The old JPG remains active; source, runtime and QA-ledger replacement, current D/P bindings, the central five-gate report and human release review require separate action.
